title: Perineural Injection for Tarsal Tunnel Syndrome: Critique of Our High-Volume Injection Technique and a Proposed Reporting Framework
content: Background: Perineural injection, local anaesthetic blockade and hydrodissection are related but distinct interventions used in the conservative management of tarsal tunnel syndrome (TTS). A 2021 technique report described nerve-stimulation-guided injection of a high-volume corticosteroid and local anaesthetic mixture as a treatment protocol. Objective: The aim of this paper is to critically reassess that report, to clarify the function of electrical localisation, and to identify a proposed checklist for future reporting of related techniques.Methods: A narrative appraisal examined selected TTS treatment, diagnostic and anatomical studies, indirect carpal tunnel evidence, peripheral nerve safety guidance and product information. Findings: While the evidence does not validate our high-volume protocol, electrical stimulation may assist needle localisation but does not demonstrate tissue-plane separation. Our 2021 report contains a volume-reporting inconsistency, and current product information advises against mixing the identified corticosteroid suspension with other fluids. Future reports should specify the anatomical target, product-specific formulation, dose, delivered volume, observed perineural spread, systemic toxicity and prospective clinical outcomes. Conclusion: Our historical high-volume perineural injection technique provides a rationale for further investigation but does not constitute an established treatment protocol. Prospective feasibility and comparative studies are needed to evaluate reproducibility, safety and sustained clinical benefit against a prespecified comparator.
